key_insight: Bayesian model averaging generally improved accuracy and calibration under distribution shift in rodent sleep scoring, with multi-basin methods performing best.
clinical_relevance: The findings may inform more robust biomedical time-series classifiers, but do not establish performance or clinical utility in human sleep scoring.
method: Compared nine approximate Bayesian inference methods spanning single- and multi-basin approaches.
Evaluated two neural network backbones against point-estimate baselines.
Tested shifts in genotype, laboratory, and species.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used in-distribution data and five out-of-distribution datasets, finding modest in-distribution gains and generally improved out-of-distribution accuracy and calibration.
watch_item: Benefits were not universal: Bayesian model averaging did not improve inter-rater disagreement detection.
paper_title: Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
